The 1st International Nexus Workshop on Human Roles in Software Engineering

NEXUS 2027 explores the roles of humans in software engineering and their evolving relationships with technology and with one another.

About the Workshop

Humans elicit requirements, build and test systems, share domain knowledge, exercise judgment, and make creative decisions. Large language models and autonomous agents are changing where those responsibilities begin and end.

NEXUS 2027 creates a focused forum for studying that shifting boundary: what people uniquely contribute today, how human–AI and human–human relationships change, and whether some activities inherently require human involvement.

Call for Papers

NEXUS 2027 welcomes contributions from researchers, students, and practitioners in software engineering, artificial intelligence, human-computer interaction, and related areas. We invite:

  • Original research and empirical studies on human roles in software engineering.
  • Innovative ideas and well-argued perspectives on how human work may evolve.
  • Industry experience and practical reports from AI-assisted software development.

Previously published and unpublished work

Unpublished work. Original and unpublished work is welcome. Authors may choose single-blind or double-blind review. After acceptance, authors may optionally pursue the journal publication opportunity described below.

Previously published work. Previously published work is also welcome. The submission must clearly identify the original publication. It will be reviewed through the same presentation-centered process using single-blind review and, if accepted, may be presented at the workshop but is not eligible for the journal publication opportunity.

Topics of interest

Topics include, but are not limited to:

  • Human factors across requirements, design, development, testing, and maintenance.
  • Knowledge, expertise, judgment, creativity, cognition, well-being, and skills.
  • Division of labor, oversight, validation, trust, and autonomous engineering agents.
  • Communication and collaboration among developers, users, and stakeholders.
  • Developer experience, productivity, education, and the evolving profession.

Submission Requirements

A professional video production is not expected. Reviewers will focus on the research and on clear, complete communication.

Required: recorded presentation

Submit a self-contained recorded presentation of up to 20 minutes that communicates the problem, core contributions, evidence, and limitations.

  • MP4 using the H.264 codec
  • Resolution up to 1080p
  • Maximum file size of 600 MB
  • Presentation slides in PDF format

Optional: extended abstract

Authors may submit an extended abstract of up to four pages, excluding references, as a concise written summary for reviewers.

Optional: supplementary materials

Authors may also submit a full manuscript, datasets, code, instruments, or replication packages that support the review.

Review and submission system

Authors may choose single-blind or double-blind review. Every submission will receive at least three reviews based on relevance, originality, soundness, clarity, and significance.

Submissions will be managed through HotCRP. The workshop-specific link will be posted here before submissions open on 1 December 2026.

After Acceptance

Journal opportunity

Authors of accepted unpublished work will be offered the opportunity to develop a full paper for Software Engineering Nexus. This opportunity is entirely optional: authors are not required to submit to or publish in the journal and may participate in the workshop without pursuing it. For authors who choose this route, publication is guaranteed after the journal's subsequent paper review and revision process. Under the journal's currently announced plan, each published paper receives a USD 500 honorarium and the USD 1,600 APC is waived. See the journal website.

Best Presentation Award

All on-site participants will be invited to vote anonymously for the presentation they find clearest, most engaging, and most effective in stimulating new thoughts and discussion. The winner will receive a certificate and a monetary prize.
